signals.entity: Asseco Central Europe vs Printec (Slovenska sporitelna)
signals.signal: Asseco Central Europe's 'ATM Multivendor Software' product page names Slovenska sporitelna, a.s. and DanubePay, a.s. as its references. The product is explicitly built on the KAL Kalignite platform, installs on devices from 30+ ATM manufacturers, and covers withdrawal, deposit and recycling, contactless and cardless operations, kiosk services, VAS/third-party services and visually-impaired operation.
signals.source_name: Asseco Central Europe - ATM Multivendor Software (product page)
signals.implies: Direct, documented displacement risk to Printec's NCR/Atleos APTRA application layer and multivendor managed services at SLSP - Asseco offers the same KAL Kalignite stack Erste already uses at Ceska sporitelna. Printec must defend on hardware, cash-cycle optimisation (OptiCash), FLM/managed services and recycler expertise rather than on the ATM application alone.
signals.followup: Establish which SLSP ATM estate runs Asseco/KAL vs APTRA, and whether the 2026 'new ATM types' work is a full application replacement

signals.entity: Asseco Central Europe - Slovak banking client list
signals.signal: Asseco Central Europe's banking references page lists Ceska sporitelna, Ceskoslovenska obchodni banka, Diebold Nixdorf, EXIMBANKA SR, Magyar Nemzeti Bank, Moneta Money Bank, Postova banka, Slovenska sporitelna, Tatra banka, UniCredit Bank Slovakia and Vseobecna uverova banka.
signals.implies: Asseco has an existing commercial relationship with essentially every bank in the Slovak cluster - and counts Diebold Nixdorf itself as a client. This is a cluster-wide competitive threat to Printec's software/services position, not an SLSP-only issue.
signals.followup: Determine per-bank scope of each Asseco relationship (core, cards, ATM app)

signals.signal: RE-VERIFICATION: the 26/06/2026 date attached to 'SLSP switches ATM-system software development to Asseco' traces to a joint Asseco/SLSP media event on 26/06/2026 covered by TOUCHIT.sk. The Asseco press release issued from that event (dated Bratislava 26/06/2026, published 03/07/2026) is a market-trends piece by Asseco IT analyst Filip Vojtek and announces NO contract, scope or value. The only Asseco-SLSP link in the TOUCHIT article is a photo caption, 'New ATM types in Asseco's development environment'. No award notice exists (SLSP is private, so not in UVO).
signals.source_name: Asseco Central Europe press release / TOUCHIT.sk
signals.implies: Do not brief internally that Printec has lost an SLSP contract. The verified threat is structural (Asseco is an SLSP ATM-software reference on KAL Kalignite) rather than a newly announced award.
signals.followup: Ask Printec SK account team to confirm current APTRA vs Asseco split at SLSP

signals.signal: At the 26/06/2026 event SLSP disclosed ~350 recycling ATMs deployed since 2015; availability >99% for classic ATMs and ~98.5% for recyclers, with jams from creased notes/foreign objects the main cause of outage; each ATM carries a 'passport' of ~30 accessibility/technical attributes used to steer network modernisation; audio-jack voice guidance for visually impaired clients; NFC withdrawal saves 5-6 seconds; preferred-amount and denomination-choice personalisation; cashback at ~3,000 checkouts with the limit raised from EUR 50 to EUR 100 in 2025; ~half of all ATM withdrawals are EUR 100 or less. SLSP says it is inspired by Nordic SHARED ATM networks.
signals.implies: Recycler fleet up from ~290 to ~350; the 98.5% recycler availability gap and jam-driven outages are a direct managed-services/FLM and note-validator opportunity for Printec, as is the accessibility-driven modernisation programme.
signals.followup: Confirm the 350 figure and current deposit/withdrawal split in the SLSP 2025 annual report

signals.signal: Slovakia had approximately 3,300 ATMs in H1-2025, about 616 ATMs per million inhabitants - the highest density among its neighbours (Poland led on absolute count with ~20,600). About 45% of Slovak ATMs accepted contactless cards versus a eurozone average of ~34%. Globally ~2.9m ATMs in 2025 (down from ~3.3m in 2017) still handling ~87bn transactions a year; ~1m recycling ATMs in 2024 (about one third of all devices) forecast to exceed 1.2m by 2029; contactless was ~42% of new installations.
signals.source_name: Asseco Central Europe press release 'Bankomat nezanika. Meni sa na inteligentny financny terminal'
signals.implies: Sizes the Slovak addressable fleet at ~3,300 units with ~55% still not contactless - a concrete upgrade/replacement pipeline for Printec hardware and software.
signals.followup: Cross-check the 3,300 figure against NBS/ECB payment statistics

signals.signal: Tatra banka operates 355 deposit-capable devices processing approximately 450,000 deposits per month; cap of 200 notes per door-opening (repeatable up to the depositor limit), EUR 50,000 per account per day and EUR 10,000 per person per day. Clients may deposit to any Tatra banka or Raiffeisen banka account, including via a branch-generated QR code.
signals.implies: Deposit fleet is up from the 259 previously known - the 'Bankomat 2.0' replacement of withdrawal-only units is well advanced. Recycler hardware, cash forecasting/OptiCash and managed services demand.
signals.followup: Confirm Tatra banka total ATM count and remaining withdrawal-only units in the 2025 annual report

signals.entity: Slovak banking sector (VUB, SLSP, Tatra, CSOB, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, Fio)
signals.signal: Around 1,000 deposit ATMs are installed in Slovakia and today accept deposits only from the operating bank's own clients. VUB spokesman Dominik Misa: Slovak banks are already analysing how to remove this technical limitation and significantly increase the number of devices at which cash can be deposited. Asseco separately promotes shared ATM networks (Netherlands/Belgium/Sweden models) and SLSP says Nordic shared networks are an inspiration.
signals.implies: A Slovak interbank shared-deposit scheme (as already built in Czechia) would need switching, routing, reconciliation, AML monitoring and recycler upgrades - a large multi-bank Printec opportunity, and one Asseco is openly courting.
signals.followup: Check NBS and the Slovak Banking Association for a formal interbank cash-deposit interoperability project

signals.signal: VUB is progressively replacing its oldest deposit ATMs, which accept only 50 banknotes per deposit; it applies a per-client daily AML deposit limit and charges EUR 0.50 per corporate-account deposit. VUB has publicly stated its strategy is significant expansion of the deposit-ATM network and coverage of the whole territory of Slovakia.
signals.implies: Active hardware replacement cycle at VUB - direct recycler/deposit-module sales plus AML transaction-monitoring integration.
signals.followup: Obtain VUB's current deposit-ATM count and any 2026 procurement

signals.signal: UniCredit Bank SK has 56 deposit ATMs across Slovakia, deliberately sited at all business locations and also where its branches used to be, to preserve withdrawal and deposit service at those points; up to 200 notes and EUR 10,000 per deposit; deposits to third-party accounts within the bank are allowed.
signals.implies: Branch-replacement-by-recycler is the stated UniCredit SK model - each branch closure converts into a recycler placement Printec can supply and service.
signals.followup: Get an updated 2026 UniCredit SK device count

signals.signal: 365.bank states it has no deposit ATMs and is currently analysing the business case given falling cash operations; mBank does not rule out its own deposit-ATM network but says it is premature to give detail. Postova banka and Prima banka also do not offer deposit ATMs.
signals.implies: Four unserved Slovak banks - greenfield deposit/recycler opportunity, and prime candidates for a shared/outsourced deposit network (Printec managed services).
signals.followup: Re-ask 365.bank in 2026 whether the analysis concluded

signals.signal: Under Act 384/2025 Z.z. the cashless-payment obligation for purchases above EUR 1 applies from 01/05/2026 (postponed from 01/03/2026); from 01/01/2026 ALL service providers must record sales in eKasa (the previous exemption list was abolished); a new cloud 'software online registration cash register' type was introduced; sellers must display an A5-minimum notice at the point of sale. Fines for eKasa breaches are EUR 1,500-20,000 first offence and EUR 3,000-40,000 repeat; cashless-payment breaches up to EUR 1,500 first and EUR 15,000 repeat, plus possible 72-hour sales ban or licence withdrawal.
signals.implies: Every Slovak service business now needs an eKasa register AND a card-acceptance route - direct demand for Printec eKasa ECR, Android POS and acquiring enablement. Note the fine bands differ from the EUR 500-15,000 previously carried.
signals.followup: Verify fine bands against Act 384/2025 text on slov-lex.sk

signals.signal: A preventive inspection campaign runs across four risk sectors (construction trades, personal care, gastronomy/accommodation, private clinics), checking for an eKasa register, a working cashless payment option and the mandatory notice. Earlier enforcement: nearly 1,600 eKasa inspections in October 2025 with one third finding breaches and EUR 265,010 of fines; 222 inspections in the first 12 days of November 2025 with ~48.65% finding breaches. Citizens can report refused card payments.
signals.implies: Enforcement is real and rising - an urgency driver for POS/eKasa terminal sales to SME merchants, especially the newly-captured trades and clinics segments.
signals.followup: Find the Financna sprava release with 2026 inspection statistics

signals.signal: Slovenska posta's self-service kiosk deployment remains a five-branch pilot (Bratislava Namestie SNP 35 and Mlynske nivy 5A/Stanica Nivy, Kosice Humenska 4, Sturovo Hlavna 60, Zilina Sladkovicova 14) offering cash deposit and withdrawal, ePoukaz payment and Pay-by-square bill payment in cash or by card; the company says evaluation of the real-world test will determine how the concept develops. NO kiosk/self-service/ATM tender appears in Slovenska posta's public procurement record; its live 2026 tenders are a logistics information system (~EUR 13.7m ex-VAT, bids due 24/08/2026), security system support (~EUR 1.75m over three years), catering and facilities.
signals.implies: Still pre-tender - the window to shape specifications for a national post-office self-service kiosk rollout is open now. Printec kiosk, cash-recycling and bill-payment stack fits directly.
signals.followup: Monitor posta.eranet.sk and the UVO Vestnik for a kiosk notice; find the pilot evaluation date
